subject: Clarify encryption custody + logging/retention implications after our demo
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@greenbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenBank Security <security@greenbank.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up on encryption + logging concerns (post-demo)

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the demo this morning. Quick recap from GreenBank's side and a few specific asks so we can move this through procurement and InfoSec: 

Key questions we need answers for before the next review:
- Custody model: we need to confirm whether Redwood supports true BYOK with customer-controlled CMKs AND an HSM-backed option where the key material never leaves our HSM (cloud HSM or on-prem). If BYOK is supported, we need details on rotation, emergency key revocation, and whether Redwood performs any key wrapping.
- Logged data: what exactly is logged by default (request metadata, full prompt text, truncated prompt, responses, model intermediate tokens)? Can logs be redacted at ingestion so PII never reaches long-term storage?
- Retention windows: we have a regulatory requirement to retain transaction traces for 7 years, but PII must be purged from non-essential systems after 90 days. Need to understand how Redwood separates telemetry/audit trail from PII-bearing content and whether we can configure different retention windows.
- In-transit: confirm TLS versions/ciphers and if mutual TLS (mTLS) is supported for private deployments.
- Evidence: sample SOC 2 encryptions sections, HSM attestation (if using CloudHSM / Thales), and any relevant architectural diagrams.

Can you provide a short doc outlining the options (BYOK CMK, Redwood-managed keys, HSM-backed KMS), what changes in logging/retention capabilities for each option, and what pieces require us to run a Private (VPC) deployment vs. Hosted API? Also, please include a rough timeline and level-of-effort estimate for a POC where our key never leaves our custody.

Appreciate it — Oliver
Oliver Grant | VP, Platform Risk — GreenBank

Subject: Re: Follow-up on encryption + logging concerns (post-demo)

Oliver — thanks for the clear list. Good questions; summarized answers below + proposed next steps. See attached one-pager for an at-a-glance comparison.

Short answers (high level):
- Custody model: Redwood supports three tiers: Redwood-managed keys (default), BYOK via cloud KMS where you provision the CMK (we never hold the key material), and HSM-backed BYOK where key material can be generated and stored in your HSM (CloudHSM/Thales/On-prem HSM) with Redwood integrating via a KMS gateway. For the HSM option we provide attestation steps and an integration playbook.
- Key operations: rotation is configurable; with BYOK you manage rotation policies in your KMS and we honor key versions. Emergency key revocation is supported via immediate refusal of requests encrypted under revoked keys; we can show the revocation flow on a call.
- Logging: default Hosted logs include request/response metadata and truncated prompts (first 1024 chars) for debugging. For Private/VPC deployments you can choose to disable prompt persistence entirely and enable only structured telemetry (latency, token counts, route, model version). We have masking hooks at the ingestion layer for PII redaction.
- Retention: policy is configurable per deployment. Typical setup: (a) short-term working store (0–90 days, configurable) for debugging, (b) audit traces (hashes, non-PII metadata) for long-term retention (up to 7+ years). We can map your retention requirements to separate buckets so PII is purged while audit hashes are kept.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers in Hosted mode; mTLS is available for Private deployments and Dedicated nodes.
- Evidence: attaching our quick comparison PDF; will follow up with SOC 2 artifact and HSM attestation doc (internal).

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with our crypto engineer (Camila) — 60 mins. Goal: confirm HSM attestation details and KMS gateway architecture.
2) Provide Redwood encryption options doc + SOC 2 encryptions section and a redacted HSM attestation sample (Camila).
3) Decide whether PII should be prevented from entering logs (masking at ingestion) or first stored short-term and redacted later — we recommend ingestion-time masking for regulated data.
4) If GreenBank requires key material that never leaves your boundary, we propose a Private deployment POC (timeline: ~6 weeks for infra + integration, faster if we reuse an existing dedicated region).

I’ll coordinate times: Camila, can you take point on the deep-dive? Karthik — I’ll loop you in on procurement timelines once we have the spec. Stephanie — can you pull the latest SOC 2 encryptions artifacts and HSM attestation template for OLiver?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Happy to run the technical deep-dive. Quick clarifications to make the session efficient:
- Please confirm the HSM vendor(s) you're evaluating (AWS CloudHSM, Thales, Entrust, on-prem) so I can bring relevant attestation templates.
- For BYOK via Cloud KMS, do you expect to manage key rotation entirely, or would you like Redwood to coordinate rotation windows and versions?
- Can you indicate an example endpoint that should use mTLS (API ingestion, internal admin console, or both)?

What I can bring to the call:

- HSM attestation sample and CloudHSM integration checklist
- Log flow diagram showing ingestion-time masking and separate retention buckets for PII vs audit traces
- Example configuration snippets for disabling prompt persistence in Private mode

mTLS: we’d like mTLS on ingestion endpoints for the POC. Also — please confirm whether masked prompts still allow for deterministic hashing so we can preserve auditability without storing cleartext.
